title: Microsoft Teams: reactions in events with up to 100,000 attendees
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and correctly distinguishes the planned reactions expansion from the current 20,000-attendee ceiling. Its licensing and control paths are supported; minor corrections should cite the emoji description and flag the PowerShell reference's preview qualification.

claims.where: front matter: title, products; What's changing
claims.claim: The feature belongs to Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support sending reactions during Teams events with up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Teams now supports reactions in events at this scale. You can send reactions during the event

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Attendees will be able to see reactions other attendees send at that scale.
claims.quote: You can send reactions during the event and see the reactions others send, so everyone can share the moment together.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target is December CY2026, not a committed rollout date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Android, Desktop, iOS, Mac and Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac", "Web"]

claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Current Learn documentation limits reactions in events optimised for large audiences to 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: [Reactions](manage-reactions-meetings)^2^ | Up to 20,000 attendees

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: For events with 20,001 to 100,000 attendees, reactions are currently turned off in the scheduling form and organisers cannot turn them on.
claims.quote: For events with 20,001 to 100,000 attendees, this feature is turned off in the scheduling form and can't be turned on by organizers.

claims.claim: The existing meeting-policy reactions default in organisers' Meeting options is On.
claims.quote: By default, meeting reactions are set to On in your organizers' Meeting options.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Today's meeting policy sets a reactions default rather than an enforced block, and organisers can change it for each meeting and event.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can use the Teams admin center or PowerShell to set the default value for reactions in your organizers' Meeting options. Organizers can change the setting for each meeting and event they create.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the planned reactions expansion above 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions events above 20000 100000 default tenant events policy AllowMeetingReactions. Read roadmap, manage-reactions-meetings, meetings-events-feature-comparison and set-up-events; they give the current default and ceiling, not the expansion's arrival default.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the planned 100,000-attendee reactions behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions events 100000 20000 manage reactions meetings attendee capacity pack licensing; Teams reactions events above 20000 100000 default tenant events policy AllowMeetingReactions. Opened comparison, reactions, licensing and pack pages; current reactions ceiling remains 20,000.

claims.claim: The reactions default is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting engagement > Reactions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit. Under Meeting engagement, turn the Reactions toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions $false is the MicrosoftTeams PowerShell call for the reactions control.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. -AllowMeetingReactions: Set to false to disable Meeting Reactions. Type: Boolean. Default value: True. -Identity: Specify the name of the policy being created.

claims.claim: The reactions guidance prints -AllowMeetingReactions Disabled.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMeetingReactions Disabled

claims.claim: No separate tenant-wide UI or API, or events-policy setting, is documented for reactions above 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions events above 20000 100000 default tenant events policy AllowMeetingReactions. Read manage-reactions-meetings, set-up-events, Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, comparison and settings-policies-reference search excerpt; no distinct large-event reactions switch appears.

claims.claim: Town hall creation is controlled at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers with the policy from creating town halls.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled
claims.fix: Add to controls[2].note: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as still in preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps, whose introduction says 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.'

claims.claim: Disabling Events optimized for a large audience blocks town halls rather than reactions alone.
claims.quote: Events optimized for a large audience (On,Off) | -AllowTownhalls (Enabled,Disabled) | Controls whether users with this policy can create events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls.

claims.claim: Town hall audience access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: Go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests is documented for restricting town hall access.
claims.quote: To only allow users in your organization and guests to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess EveryoneInOrganizationAndGuests
claims.fix: Add to controls[3].note: 'The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as still in preview.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy?view=teams-ps, whose introduction says 'Note that this policy is currently still in preview.'

claims.claim: Who can attend events optimized for a large audience defaults to Everyone.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The events-policy audience setting governs who can attend town halls created by organisers assigned that policy.
claims.quote: Controls who can attend events optimized for large audiences (such as town halls) created by organizers with this policy.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Attendee Capacity Packs use an add-on licensing model for Teams Enterprise.
claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise that let event organizers host events for up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Hosting events above 3,000 attendees with engagement capabilities requires purchased Attendee Capacity Packs, subject to the stated legacy Teams Premium exception.
claims.quote: To host events with more than 3,000 attendees with engagement capabilities (chat, reactions, raise hand, polls, Q&A), organizations must purchase Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licenses and assign them to organizers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; controls[4]; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The capacity-pack licence is assigned to the organiser.
claims.quote: organizations must purchase Attendee Capacity Pack add-on licenses and assign them to organizers.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Attendee Capacity Packs enable event capacities up to 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise that let event organizers host events for up to 100,000 attendees.
They can be purchased to support 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 event attendees.

claims.claim: Each organiser can be assigned only one attendee pack.
claims.quote: While your organization can purchase multiple packs, each organizer can only be assigned one pack.

claims.claim: Attendee packs increase event capacity and unlock no other feature capabilities.
claims.quote: Attendee packs increase capacity for Teams events. They don't unlock any other feature capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: An active Teams Premium licence purchased before 1 April 2026 retains event capacity up to 100,000 until its current term ends.
claims.quote: Organizers with an active Teams Premium license purchased before April 1, 2026, can continue to host events for up to 100,000 attendees until their current Teams Premium term ends.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: An engaged event above 20,000 attendees needs a pack of 35,000 or more, or the described legacy Teams Premium entitlement.
claims.quote: 20K | 20,000; 35K | 35,000; 50K | 50,000; 75K | 75,000; 100K | 100,000. Organizers with an active Teams Premium license purchased before April 1, 2026, can continue to host events for up to 100,000 attendees until their current Teams Premium term ends.

claims.claim: No meter is described specifically for the reactions expansion.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions 100000 attendee capacity pack price metered licensing. Opened events-licensing, attendee-capacity-pack and attendee-capacity-pack-manage; search also returned eCDN purchasing and pricing FAQ excerpts. No reactions-expansion meter was described.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published
claims.claim: The Attendee Capacity Pack Learn pages give pack sizes but do not give prices.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions 100000 attendee capacity pack price metered licensing. Read attendee-capacity-pack and attendee-capacity-pack-manage in full, plus events-licensing; those pages specify capacities and assignment, not pack prices.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence specifically for the reactions expansion is published, beyond the documented event-capacity licensing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions 100000 attendee capacity pack price metered licensing. Read events-licensing, attendee-capacity-pack and manage-reactions-meetings; they give general event entitlements and capacity packs, not a separate expansion licence.

claims.claim: Pack assignment is at Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Assign Add-on licenses > Attendee pack.
claims.quote: Go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Licenses tab, select Assign to new users to get started. In the Assign Add-on licenses pane: For each individual user, select the pack size that you want to assign in the Attendee pack column.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense is a documented general licence-assignment operation usable for purchased Teams add-on licences.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense

claims.claim: The assignLicense request uses addLicenses objects carrying the licence skuId.
claims.quote: addLicenses | assignedLicense collection | A collection of assignedLicense objects that specify the licenses to add. "addLicenses": [{ "disabledPlans": [], "skuId": "f30db892-07e9-47e9-837c-80727f46fd3d" }]

claims.claim: The assignLicense request requires removeLicenses, which can be empty.
claims.quote: removeLicenses | Guid collection | A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.

claims.claim: Managing attendee-pack assignment in the Teams admin center requires Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Teams Administrator has read-only access to the Teams admin center License Management section.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.claim: Teams administrators can edit meeting and events policies.
claims.quote: Teams Administrator | Manage the Teams service, and manage and create Microsoft 365 Groups. | Everything in the Microsoft Teams admin center and associated PowerShell controls, including: Manage meetings, including meeting policies, configurations, and conference bridges.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events shows which organisers have attendee packs and their assigned pack sizes.
claims.quote: To see which organizers have attendee packs assigned to them: In the Teams admin center, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. Assigned pack | Size of the attendee pack assigned to the organizer.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Live reactions are emoji feedback displayed during a meeting or event.
claims.quote: Choose from a range of live reactions, including: Like [Image of the 3D emoji like reaction]. Your reaction pops up momentarily at the bottom of your meeting and over your profile picture or video feed.
claims.fix: Add https://support.microsoft.com/office/express-yourself-in-microsoft-teams-meetings-with-live-reactions-a8323a40-3d07-4129-934b-305370a36e21 to sources, titled 'Express yourself in Microsoft Teams meetings with live reactions'. The cited Manage reactions page links to this description.

claims.claim: No new data access is described for the reactions expansion.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100000 attendees reactions names emoji stream latency attendance engagement report; Teams reactions 100000 attendees sign in permissions app autonomous. Read roadmap, reactions, comparison and licensing pages; no new data-access mechanism is described for the expansion.

claims.claim: No new sign-in requirement, permission or app is described specifically for the reactions expansion.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions 100000 attendees sign in permissions app autonomous. Read roadmap, manage-reactions-meetings, comparison and events-licensing; the expansion names no new identity or app requirement. General events service-protection eOTP is not a new reactions requirement.

claims.claim: The described capability consists of attendees sending reactions, not autonomous actions.
claims.quote: You can send reactions during the event and see the reactions others send, so everyone can share the moment together.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how the reactions expansion affects stream quality or latency at 100,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams 100000 attendees reactions names emoji stream latency attendance engagement report; "reactions" "100,000" latency stream. Read roadmap, comparison and Ultra-Low Latency FAQ excerpt; no quality or latency effect attributable to the reactions expansion is stated.

claims.claim: Ultra-Low Latency is currently documented for events up to 20,000 attendees.
claims.quote: [Ultra-Low Latency](ultra-low-latency-streaming-events) | Up to 20,000 attendees

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described whether attendees of the planned events above 20,000 see the identities of reaction senders.
claims.quote: Searched: "reactions" "town hall" "names" "100,000"; Teams 100000 attendees reactions names emoji stream latency attendance engagement report. Read comparison, reactions and live-reactions support page; meeting profile-picture behaviour is stated, not identity display for this planned larger-event case.

claims.claim: No source says existing reactions behaviour changes before the roadmap target.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams reactions events above 20000 100000 default tenant events policy AllowMeetingReactions. Read roadmap, manage-reactions-meetings, comparison and set-up-events; none states a pre-target change to the existing reactions behaviour.
